Definition: Abijam (or Abijah), a king of Judah
BiblicalUsage: Abijam — also called Abijah — is the son of Rehoboam who reigns three years in Jerusalem, and the text is blunt: ‘he walked in all the sins of his father’; yet ‘for David’s sake did the LORD his God give him a lamp in Jerusalem.’ His wars with Jeroboam are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah.
TheologicalSignificance: A bad king kept on the throne for David's sake — not his own. I believe Abijam shows me how God's promise outlasts a man's failure: the lamp in Jerusalem burns because of a covenant God made with David, and no son's sin can put out what God has promised to keep.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
